issues.legal_issue: A deduction for development is not automatically required when valuing a large acquired tract by comparison with sales of smaller plots if the acquired land is already suitable for the same use and requires little or no further development.
material_facts: The land was acquired for housing and road purposes, and the lower court valued it by reference to comparable sales of smaller plots.
The acquired land was level, suitable for construction without levelling or reclamation, and had access to roads and other amenities.
The land was adjacent to developed areas and could be used as building sites with little or no further development.
The High Court deducted one-third of the comparable value solely on the basis that a large area had been acquired.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was wrong to deduct one-third of the value. The appeals were allowed, and compensation was restored to the amount determined by the subordinate court, with interest and solatium in accordance with law.
issues.legal_principle: In determining market value in land acquisition proceedings, the price of smaller comparable plots may be used, with a deduction ordinarily considered for the expenses and land needed to develop a larger tract. The deduction depends on all relevant circumstances and is not justified merely because the acquired area is large. Where the larger tract is suitably located, already developed with relevant amenities, fit for the same building use as the comparable plots, and needs little or no further development, no development deduction is warranted. The Court distinguished Tribeni Devi v. Collector, Ranchi, AIR 1972 SC 1417, and relied on Kaushalya Devi v. Land Acquisition Officer, [1984] 2 SCR 900; Administrator General of West Bengal v. Collector, Varanasi, AIR 1988 SC 943; and Special Tahsildar, Land Acquisition, Vishakapatnam v. Smt. A. Mangala Gowri, 1991 (2) Scale 301. The proceedings arose from a reference under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, concerning land acquired following notifications under Section 4(1); the judgment does not separately analyze Section 24.

rule.if: land_acquisition_compensation_case and small_plot_comparables and acquired_tract_suitable_for_same_use and developed_amenities_available and little_or_no_further_development_needed

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_case: A court is determining compensation for land acquired through a compulsory land acquisition proceeding.
predicates.small_plot_comparables: The valuation relies on genuine sales of smaller plots as comparable transactions.
predicates.acquired_tract_suitable_for_same_use: The acquired tract can be used for the same purpose as the smaller comparable plots.
predicates.developed_amenities_available: The acquired tract is in a developed setting and has access to relevant amenities such as roads and services.
predicates.little_or_no_further_development_needed: The acquired tract requires little or no further work to make it suitable for the intended use.

issues.definition: When compensation for acquired land is assessed using smaller plot sales, these predicates mean that the acquired tract should not have a development deduction if it is already suitable for the same use, has relevant amenities, and needs little or no further development.
